<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par113 />may form part of certain combinations (as a subject, predicate, or object, or even as a genitive,<ref>The infinitive absolute can never be joined with a genitive or a pronominal suffix.</ref> see below); but such a use of the infinitive absolute (instead of the infinitive construct with or without a preposition) is, on the whole, rare, and, moreover, open to question on critical grounds. On the other hand, the infinitive absolute frequently exhibits its character as an expression of the {{GHGterm|verbal idea}} by taking an object, either in the accusative or even with a preposition.

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|b}}
Examples of the use of the infinitive absolute:—

(''a'') As subject, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=27}} {{GHGheb|text=אָכֹל דְּבַשׁ הַרְבּוֹת לֹא טוֹב|translate=it is not good to eat much honey}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=10|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=4|verse=17}}; epexegetically, after a demonstrative pronoun, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=58|verse=5}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=14|verse=12}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|c}}
(''b'') As predicate, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=32|verse=17}} ''and the effect of righteousness'' (is) {{GHGheb|text=הַשְׁקֵט וָבֶ֫טַח|translate=quietness}} (prop. to ''find rest'') ''and confidence''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|d}}
(''c'') As object, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=לִמְדוּ הֵיטֵב|translate=learn to do well}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=15|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=18}}; according to the sense also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=23}} 23:14, as well as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=5}} ({{GHGheb|text=הָסֵר}} and {{GHGheb|text=פָּרֹץ}} virtually depend on the idea of the wish contained in {{GHGheb|text=עֹשֶׂה}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=13}}, where a long series of infinitives absolute is governed by {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה}}, and 59:13 (six infinitives governed by {{GHGheb|text=יְדַֽעֲנוּם}} in verse 12); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=56}} is strange since the object precedes the infinitive absolute which governs it,<ref>Perhaps {{GHGheb|text=הַצֵּג}} according to {{GHGpar|53|k}} should be explained as an infinitive construct, or should be written {{GHGheb|text=הַצִּג}}.</ref> also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=24}}, where the statement of place precedes the infinitive absolute.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=3}} the infinitive absolute as the object of the verb is placed before it for the sake of emphasis (with the verb negatived by {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=57|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=23}}), so also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=3|verse=45}} where it is the remoter object and co-ordinated with a substantive.

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|e}}
(''d'') As genitive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=23}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּמַטְאֲטֵא הַשְׁמֵד|translate=with the besom of destruction}}; so perhaps also 4:4 {{GHGheb|text=בְּרוּחַ בָּעֵר}}; cf. further, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=21|verse=16|hidebook=1}}. The infinitive absolute is never used in immediate connexion with prepositions<ref>{{GHGheb|text=ואחרי שָׁתֹה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=9}} is impossible Hebrew, and as the LXX shows, a late addition.</ref> (which as being originally substantives govern the genitive), but always the infinitive construct; but if a second infinitive is co-ordinated by {{GHGheb|text=וְ}} with such an infinitive construct, it has the form of the infinitive absolute (since it is released from the immediate government of the preposition), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=22|verse=13}} ... {{GHGheb|text=בְּתִתְּךָ לוֹ לֶחֶם וְשָׁאוֹל לוֹ בֵּֽאלֹהִים|translate=in that thou hast given him bread ... and hast enquired of God for him}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=36|verse=3}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=26}}, 33 (after {{GHGheb|text=מִן}}); after {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=7|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=44|verse=17|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|f}}
(''e'') Governing an accusative of the object, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=הָרֹג בָּקָר וְשָׁחֹם צאֹן|translate=slaying oxen and killing sheep}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=30|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=5|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=23|verse=30}}, and of the examples in ''a–d'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=56}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=58|verse=6|hidebook=1}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=27}}, &c.; followed by a preposition, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=מָאוֹס בָּרָע וּבָחוֹר בַּטּוֹב|translate=to refuse the evil and choose the good}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=15|verse=12}} ({{GHGheb|text=הוֹכֵחַ לוֹ}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|g}}
If the object be a personal pronoun, then, since the infinitive absolute can never be united with a suffix (see the note on ''a''), it is affixed by means of the accusative-sign {{GHGheb|text=אֵת}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֹת}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=23}} {{GHGheb|text=וְיָדוֹעַ אֹתִי|translate=and knoweth me}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=36|verse=3}}.<section end=par113 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
